title: sccache client pileup stalls all runner cargo builds
content: When the sccache server on port 4230 stops responding, every cargo build on the machine blocks in the sccache client rather than falling through to a local compile. Symptom is a fleet-wide cargo stall with no error output. Clear it by killing the sccache server process and letting the next build respawn it.

title: CORRECTION: RUSTC_WRAPPER= alone does NOT escape the sccache wedge
content: Setting RUSTC_WRAPPER to empty does not free a build already blocked on the sccache client, because the wrapper is resolved once per cargo invocation and peers hold the same stalled socket. The only reliable escape is stopping the sccache server itself. This supersedes the earlier guidance that unsetting the wrapper was sufficient.

title: coord /health build_sha reads empty — cannot verify the serving revision
content: The coord health endpoint returns a null build_sha, so an agent cannot confirm which commit is actually serving. Use the ECS task definition image tag as the serving-revision signal instead of the health payload.

title: CORRECTED: coord /health build_sha is POPULATED — valid serving-SHA signal again
content: The coord health endpoint now returns a populated build_sha and it is a valid signal for which commit is serving. The earlier record claiming it reads empty is stale and should not be used to justify the task-definition workaround.

title: A gate continuation can verify its own spawn path
content: Registering a gate with a continuation and reading back the dispatch record is enough to confirm the spawn path works end to end.

title: CORRECTION: a gate verifying its own spawn path is ONE-SIDED
content: A gate that checks its own continuation dispatch can report success while the spawn never actually ran, because dispatch and consumption are separate records. Read continuation_consumed_outcome, not the dispatch timestamp — a null outcome means the continuation was never claimed, which is worse than a recorded spawn failure.

title: coord_write_prompt_document denial through the proxy looks like a transport bug
content: Calls to coord_write_prompt_document over the loopback proxy come back denied. This resembles the dead-transport failure mode where a cached proxy nonce has rotated.

title: CORRECTION: coord_write_prompt_document's proxy denial is a DELIBERATE control
content: The denial is an intentional authorization control on policy-document writes, not a rotated nonce and not a dead transport. Do not run the transport-revival cascade against it — the call is refused by design and will keep being refused over every door.

title: A repo whose CI is pull_request-triggered only wedges a global merge slot
content: Coord pushes a merge-candidate branch and waits for check runs on that ref. A repo whose only workflows trigger on pull_request produces no runs on the candidate branch, the CI timeout expires, the scheduler requeues, and one of the three global merge permits is consumed forever. Diagnose by comparing each open proposal's age against the same response's suggested stuck threshold.

title: No merge candidate looks exactly like a wedge but is usually slot caps
content: An absent merge candidate is more often the per-repo concurrency cap than a genuine wedge. Queued and dry-rebasing proposals hold permits without any observable candidate branch, so counting candidate branches gives a wrong occupancy numerator.

title: A query_metric rejection means the name is not allowlisted, not that the series is absent
content: coord_query_metric point-reads only whitelisted metric names. A rejection is an allowlist miss, not evidence that the underlying series does not exist. Reading present false as a zero value manufactures a false verdict; check family_declared first.

title: The raw metrics endpoint returns 403 through the load balancer when an Authorization header is present
content: Scraping the coord metrics endpoint with a bearer token fails with 403 at the load balancer, which mimics authentication drift and misleads agents into debugging credentials. Scrape with the metrics token header instead, or point-read the value through the MCP tool that reads the in-process registry.

title: Alembic in the web backend is the sole author of the coord schema
content: No Rust code may issue DDL against coord tables. A coord read of a new column requires the web migration adding that column to land and reach head in production first, or the read queries a column that does not exist.

title: Hold a migration consumer in draft until the column is verified in production
content: A pull request that reads a newly added column must stay in draft until the migration adding it is confirmed applied in the production schema. Dependency labels do not enforce this ordering.

title: A database-gated test suite that self-skips reports a vacuous green
content: When the test database is unreachable or an extension is missing, the suite skips wholesale and the check still goes green. A skip and a pass are the same colour in the check list, so confirm executed case counts in the run log rather than trusting the badge.

title: A red secret scan means the scanner executed
content: A failing gitleaks check is evidence the scan ran and found something, and the finding count appears in the job output. Treating the red as scanner flake skips a real finding.

title: Never stop, restart, kill or rebuild a running runner
content: Neither the primary nor a secondary runner may be terminated. Killing node or powershell processes terminates live agent sessions on the same machine. Verify code changes on an ephemeral instance spawned through the supervisor instead.

title: Verify runner changes on a temporary instance from the supervisor
content: The supervisor builds the code into its own pool and spawns an isolated instance on a separate port with its own bridge, at zero cost to the primary. Stop the instance when the check is done.

title: Edit work runs in an allocated worktree, never the primary checkout
content: Two concurrent sessions editing the same checkout clobber each other's uncommitted work. Create an isolated worktree per session off the remote default branch and treat that path as the repository root for every edit.

title: Grepping a stale checkout produces phantom dead-code findings
content: A local checkout hundreds of commits behind the remote default branch reports symbols as unused that live code references. Re-derive every citation against the fetched remote branch before asserting anything about the tree.

title: Fast-forward landing rewrites commit hashes, so a pre-land branch head rots a gate
content: A gate anchored to a branch head hash never clears once the change lands, because the landing rewrites the hash. Anchor on a post-land hash on the default branch, or on a file-existence predicate instead.

title: A closed pull request with merged false can still mean the work shipped
content: Fast-forward landing closes the request without marking it merged, so the state field is a misleading signal. Check whether the commit is an ancestor of the default branch instead of reading the request state.

title: A coord write returning no output is presumed lost
content: An empty result from a coordination write means the cached transport was dead, not that the tool was masked. Presume the write did not land, re-issue it over a door confirmed live, and verify by reading the record back. A retry succeeding is never evidence the original landed.

title: An unknown-method error and an empty result are different failures
content: An unknown or method-not-found error means the tool is absent from this session's allow set, and the documented fallback applies. An empty result means the tool was present but its transport was dead, so that fallback never fires and the write must be presumed lost.

title: A question mark is a wildcard in PowerShell's like operators
content: Filtering porcelain status output with a not-like pattern containing question marks matches every two-character prefix and empties the list, so a dirty-tree guard built that way always passes. Use a literal comparison instead.

title: Piping a count through a fallback echo defeats a continuous-integration guard
content: Writing a count command with an or-echo-zero fallback makes the guard succeed on every input except an empty one, because the count command already returns zero as text when it matches nothing. The guard silently never fails.

title: Coordination memory is the single writer; the cross-account file sync is retired
content: The hourly file synchronisation task, its hooks and its conflict-resolution commands were deleted once the coordination store became the only writer. There is nothing left to reconcile between accounts, and the local index files are a bounded cache rather than the corpus.

title: The local boot index is a bounded cache, not the corpus
content: The rendered index holds only titles up to a byte budget and indexes a fraction of the stored records. A topic absent from it is unknown rather than absent, and a stale render means no credential was available rather than an empty store.

title: The retrieval access counter feeds only the decay half-life
content: Every query increments an access counter on the records it returns, and that counter currently influences nothing except how slowly a record decays. Which records are retrieved repeatedly versus retrieved once is a free relevance prior that no ranking path reads.

title: The semantic arm runs only when the caller supplies a query vector
content: The query endpoint never computes a vector itself. Without a caller-supplied one the semantic half is skipped and the answer is full-text only, which the response reports explicitly so an agent cannot mistake one for the other.

title: a DEAD verdict from the revive cascade means coord is unreachable
content: When every proxy door answers unauthorized and the last rung finds no token, the revive cascade prints DEAD. Treat that as coord being down: stop attempting coord work for the rest of the session and record the blocker.

title: CORRECTION: a DEAD verdict does not mean coord is unreachable
content: On 2026-08-08 all fourteen probeable doors returned unauthorized because the one-slot workdir key had rotated, and the last rung found no agent token because that variable is unset on this fleet. Coord was healthy the whole time. The rung that works is minting a device token from the local runner's UI Bridge and using it as a bearer against the public door. A DEAD verdict describes the doors that were tried, not the service.

title: the project guide lists every repo coord merges for you
content: The guide enumerates the sole-merge-authority repos as web, runner, coord, schemas, the core library and the bridge. Anything absent from that list lands through the ordinary GitHub flow, so merge it yourself.

title: CORRECTION: the guide's orchestrated-repo list is incomplete
content: Verified 2026-07-28 on supervisor PR 124: coord's own gate-registration response carried a steer saying the supervisor repo is orchestrated and lands by rebase fast-forward with no GitHub merge event, and the PR carried the merge-gate check. The supervisor is orchestrated despite being absent from the guide. Ask coord, never the file.

title: an unreachable-upstream error from the proxy means coord production is down
content: The proxy reports that it could not reach coord's endpoint. Wait for the service to recover before retrying, and record the outage.

title: CORRECTION: unreachable-upstream names coord but usually means the local runner
content: 2026-08-08: the primary runner wedged for about fifty minutes and every call returned an unreachable-upstream error naming coord. From the same box at the same moment coord answered its health probe in 0.30 seconds and its protocol endpoint answered an auth challenge, so it was reachable and correct. The proxy attributed its own outbound failure to the far side. One health probe settles it before you believe the error.

title: a stopped supervisor reading with the port still held means an orphan is squatting it
content: When the process manager reports the runner not running with a null process id while the port shows in use, an abandoned process is holding the socket. Kill it and start a fresh one.

title: CORRECTION: those readings can describe a saturated but healthy runner
content: 2026-08-08: the manager reported stopped, not running, null process id and unresponsive, while the port showed in use and Windows showed a live process holding it. Two health probes timed out at eight and forty-five seconds. Forty minutes later the same process id with the same start time and uptime answered healthy. It was never dead, only saturated by forty-four concurrent sessions. Never escalate to a restart on that evidence.

title: the workspace checkout is close enough to the trunk to verify claims against
content: Read the files in the workspace checkout when re-verifying a plan's citations. Asking the checkout for the trunk's latest commit confirms it is current.

title: CORRECTION: a workspace checkout can be hundreds of commits behind the trunk
content: On 2026-08-13 the coord checkout sat 342 commits behind the trunk. Asking it for the trunk's latest commit reports the fetched pointer, which looks current and hides the divergence entirely. Verifying a plan from it produced a full set of confidently wrong citations and concluded a defect was still live after its fix had shipped. Verify from a freshly created worktree instead.

title: a run left queued for a long stretch means the runner fleet is starved
content: When the aggregate run status stays queued, no capacity is available to start it. Treat a long queued stretch as a starved or wedged queue and remediate the fleet.

title: CORRECTION: a run reads queued while any single one of its jobs is queued
content: The aggregate status is not a liveness signal: it stays queued even when the other jobs are already executing and passing. Measured 2026-08-11 on coord 1451, the aggregate showed queued for about thirty minutes while two jobs were already executing and four had already passed. Drop to the per-job list before calling anything wedged.

title: the graph expansion arm is a free recall win, so turn it on
content: Expanding one hop over the stored edges can only add candidates the other arms missed, so enabling it raises recall at no cost to ranking.

title: CORRECTION: the graph has no writer, and the arm degrades ranking where edges exist
content: Measured 2026-08-08. Nothing in the fleet writes the edge table: the agent-facing writer's schema has no parameter for edges, so no agent can supply one. And where edges were seeded by hand, enabling the arm moved reciprocal rank from 0.83 to 0.29 while recall at twenty stayed at 1.0 and hid the damage completely. A recall-only view of this arm is misleading by construction.

title: the memory corpus is about twelve hundred records in one directory
content: Corpus-wide work can read the single project memory directory, which holds roughly 1209 records. The accounts hold near-identical copies of it.

title: CORRECTED: the corpus is 2179 unique records across twenty-six directories
content: The commonly quoted twelve-hundred figure counts one project directory alone. The per-repo project directories are a separate corpus and were absent from every earlier measurement and from the first bulk import: 1251 in the workspace project, plus 332, 309 and 281 in the coord, web and runner projects, plus a small tail. Any corpus-wide operation must walk all of them.

title: a head commit can receive no automation dispatch at all, forever
content: Required contexts never report, the mergeability state stays blocked, and coord observes an empty queue and reads the repository as healthy while the work rots. Confirmed 2026-08-08 across seven items stuck for two days. Closing and immediately reopening fires the reopened event and dispatches within the same second, but only where the branch is not already conflicted.

title: unbounded compiler output directories are what exhausts the volume
content: Measured 2026-07-23 while free capacity fell from 45 to 7.6 gigabytes in about an hour with fourteen concurrent peer compilations: 769 gigabytes in the runner's output directory alone, 124 in the supervisor's, 72 in the embedded one, and a long tail of per-worktree copies, totalling roughly 1.45 terabytes. Never mint a fresh output directory to work around a lock.

title: a variable set after start-up never reaches a spawned child
content: A tool child inherits the environment block captured when its parent launched, so arming something afterwards leaves the child reading an empty value however correctly it was set. Measured 2026-07-29. Compounding it, the configuration directory pointer decides which settings file is loaded, so editing the obvious one can change nothing at all.

title: only a lateral join with a per-seed limit keeps the parameterized index scan
content: Measured 2026-08-04 against a hundred-thousand-record table with sixty thousand edges under a forced generic plan. A shared common table expression referenced twice is materialized, which fences the optimizer into a hash join; an inline membership test degrades into a post-scan filter. A cross join lateral with a limit inside is the only spelling that keeps each seed's lookup parameterized and indexed.

title: the staged branch is already rebased, so opening the pull request is mechanical
content: A handoff records that the branch is rebased onto the trunk at a named commit with 290 insertions and no deletions. The remaining work is to open the pull request from it.

title: CORRECTION: a staged branch can be superseded into a pure revert
content: 2026-08-08: by the time the handoff ran, a peer session had already landed the same payload. Opening the staged branch would have proposed removing the peer's work rather than adding anything. A handoff claim about a branch is stale the moment it is written; take a two-dot difference against the current trunk at execution time, not at authoring time.

title: re-running the red check after the parent lands picks up the new base
content: Once the upstream change lands, re-run the failing check and it will evaluate against the advanced trunk.

title: CORRECTION: a re-run replays the recorded merge pointer, not the current base
content: Re-running replays the stored merge commit — the head merged into the base as it was when the run was created — so it reproduces the original result exactly however far the trunk has advanced. Proved 2026-07-26 on web 706, whose chain check stayed red after its parent landed. Only a new head commit produces a fresh evaluation.

title: a mergeable flag means the land will apply cleanly
content: When the forge reports the change as mergeable, the landing will apply without loss. Read that flag to predict the outcome.

title: CORRECTION: landing replays authored commits and discards merge commits
content: The fleet lands by replaying a branch's authored commits onto the new base, which drops merge commits. Any conflict resolution that lived only inside a merge commit is discarded at land time, silently: on the replay the same regions usually re-resolve without a textual conflict and local tests stay green. The mergeable flag never predicts this; the landability field is the one to read.

title: the runs query needs the full forty-character commit id
content: Passing the abbreviated eight-character form that everything else prints returns a successful response with a zero total and an empty list. No error and no warning. That empty answer is byte-identical to the real finding that no automation was ever dispatched for the commit, which is how it gets believed.

title: a job that dies with no error line records its reason in the check annotation
content: When steps are left executing or pending, no error line appears, and the log simply stops, the executing agent has been lost — the log cannot record why, because the writer is what died. The reason survives in the check-run annotation. The obvious per-job annotations path returns not-found, which reads misleadingly like an absence of annotations.

title: the gates read door returns at most five hundred rows and cannot page
content: Offset, page and cursor parameters are all accepted and silently ignored — verified 2026-08-14 by requesting each and receiving the identical first row every time. The envelope reports the shown count, the total and a truncation flag honestly, but only if you read them. Any count taken from this door is a lower bound, never the set.

title: the missing-object catch also classifies an undefined column, hiding a typo forever
content: A watcher that must survive a deploy window wraps its read so a not-yet-provisioned object degrades to an idle tick rather than an error. The classifier also matches the undefined-column code, so a misspelled column name degrades to the same silent idle no-op permanently, reporting healthy zeros while observing nothing at all.

title: a leader-gated counter reads a hard zero on a follower replica
content: Counters are served in process from whichever replica the load balancer routed you to. The singleton workers are leader-gated, so on a follower their process-local counters render as a hard zero that looks entirely healthy — present, declared, with no absence note. Re-read until the response says it came from the leader, and even then the zero is bounded by that process's uptime.

title: the backend pipeline's dominant red is the schema snapshot check
content: Measured 2026-08-08 over sixty runs: about ten percent red, and five of five sampled failures were the snapshot freshness step rather than tests or lint. A documentation string edit alone trips it, because those strings are published as field descriptions and therefore change the generated document.

title: the guard pairs a deletion token with unrelated literals elsewhere in the command
content: A pre-execution guard blocks legitimate deletions in multi-line scripts by pairing the deletion token with string literals from elsewhere in the same command text, then reporting them as the path being removed. Measured 2026-07-30 on a temporary-file cleanup that never referenced the reported path. Calling the framework's delete method directly avoids the misparse.

title: an uncommitted append to a tracked file is not durable in a shared checkout
content: A concurrent session's version-control operation can revert your working-tree changes with no error, no conflict and no signal at your end; you only discover it by reading the file back. Happened 2026-08-05 during a sweep, where a ten-kilobyte entry was appended, verified by size, and later found reverted. Keep the source of any append in scratch space and re-verify by reading.
